messages.subject: Detection history with the number of animals instead of presence/absence
parts:
Hi Jurgen,

Is it possible to generate a spreadsheet like species Detection History, but, instead of presence (1) / absence (0), the cells contain the number of animals per occasion i.e. count data (0, 1, 2,3,4,...). If yes, what would be the best way to do that? Looking forward to your reply. Thanks.

Hi Jurgen,

I'm assuming that this output= "count" sums up the number of detections of a species in a given length of the occasion. Let say there is more than one animal in the photos (e.g. a family of pigs), how could I include that information into my Detection History? Thanks.

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Detection history with the number of animals instead of presence/absence
parts:
Hi, 
yes, output = "count" returns the number of records (rows in your record table) during a specific occasion. 
There is no built-in function to sum up the number of individuals in addition to that. 
A workaround may be to replicate the respective rows as many times as there are individuals. 

Here's the basic idea: 

example(data.frame)
d[rep(seq.int(1,nrow(d)), times = d$y),]

where d is your record table and d$y is the number of individuals in each image. It must be 1 or higher, and must be defined for each picture.
I didn't test it though.
Let us know if it works please.
Jürgen

Hi Nico,
no problem, you can set up your tag structure as suggested, with separate tags for Species and number of individuals. recordTable will extract all metadata tags automatically, so that the tagged information about species and number of individuals will be in your record table. 
Cheers,
